title: Synthetic burst regression harness & hw-economics for A10/L4/A100/H100
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Objective: Build a reproducible synthetic-burst load harness that exercises token-level throughput and tail latency (p95, p99) across the hardware matrix (A10, L4, A100, H100) and produce normalized cost-per-token reports that include batching, KV-cache warmup effects, and spot/preemptible pricing. Deliverables: 1) harness code and job templates; 2) regression detector for p95 drift (EWMA + control chart); 3) cost-per-token estimator and comparison spreadsheet; 4) dashboard with annotated runs and automated alerts.

Methodology: Runs use a weighted prompt distribution (70% short chat-bursts: 64-256 tokens, 20% medium: 512-1024, 10% long: 2048) to emulate mixed real-world PLG traffic. Each run follows: cold KV-cache start, 10-minute warmup, 30-minute sustained burst (sustained QPS target per GPU depending on target occupancy), then 15-minute recovery. We sweep three batch policies: minimal (1-4), balanced (8-16), aggressive (32+ where supported). Metrics: tokens/sec (aggregate and per-GPU), p50/p90/p95/p99 latency for first token and per-token, queue depth, GPU occupancy, power draw, and cost per 1M tokens under on-demand and preemptible pricing.

Regression detection: Implemented an EWMA on p95 with lambda=0.3 and a control chart that adapts to variance observed during baseline window (7 runs). Alerts trigger on 3-sigma breaches or persistent 5%+ EWMA increase for 10 consecutive runs. To reduce false positives due to distribution shift, we compute the weighted average sequence length and compare against baseline; if the distribution shifts >10% the run is flagged for manual review rather than automatic rollback.

Initial run summary (seq-len mix above, balanced batching):
- A10: 22,400 tokens/sec, p95 first-token = 310ms, cost-per-1M-tokens (on-demand) = $0.29
- L4: 38,700 tokens/sec, p95 = 210ms, cost-per-1M-tokens = $0.18
- A100: 115,000 tokens/sec, p95 = 95ms, cost-per-1M-tokens = $0.074
- H100: 198,000 tokens/sec, p95 = 78ms, cost-per-1M-tokens = $0.049
Notes: H100 shows best raw tokens/sec and lowest cost/token at high occupancy but exhibits larger variance in p99 during long-seq tails; A100 provides a good balance of latency stability and cost. L4 performs surprisingly well on short-burst workloads due to memory-optimized kernel paths. A10 remains the cost-effective option for low-throughput or small teams.

Economic model: cost-per-token calculation factors: hourly machine price (on-demand/preemptible), average tokens/sec observed, GPU utilization penalty for <40% occupancy, and amortized networking + storage delta. We attach a parametric sheet so product/finance can change hourly prices and occupancy penalties.

Open questions / trade-offs: 1) How aggressively should we prefer preemptible VMs in Dedicated sizing recommendations? 2) Thresholds for automatic rollback vs. canary hold need PM sign-off (risk tolerance). 3) Do we include energy (kWh) as a visible input for enterprise customers?

Next steps: finalize harness config templates, harden regression detector to ignore controlled model/sequence shifts, run full matrix (3 repeats each) during off-peak for baseline, and create a console dashboard with run annotations and auto-generated PR with recommended pricing guidance for each customer profile.
